trust.title: How records work
trust.lead: ShaidaGo shows public records about projects, each with the sources it came from. This page explains how to read them and what they do not tell you.

classes.heading: Kinds of information
classes.intro: Every statement is labelled with the kind of information it comes from.
classes.official_source: Published by a public body, such as a government publication, budget, or procurement record.
classes.independent_source: Published by someone independent of the project, such as a newspaper or a research group.
classes.community_evidence_reviewed: Sent by a community member and checked by a person before it was added.
classes.community_report_unverified: Sent by a community member and not checked. It is never part of a public record until a person reviews it.
classes.ai_generated_explanation: Written by an automated tool to explain something. It is not a source and is always labelled.

states.heading: How well a statement is supported
states.intro: A label describes support, not a verdict about any person or organisation.
states.awaiting_verification: The statement has a source but has not yet been checked against a second one.
states.verified_official: An official source states it directly.
states.corroborated: More than one source supports it.
states.community_reviewed: A person reviewed community evidence for it.
states.disputed: Sources disagree. Both sides are shown.
states.outdated: It may no longer be true. The date it was last checked is shown.

citations.heading: Citations and dates
citations.body: Every statement links to the source it came from, with the exact passage, where it appears in the source, and the date it was last checked. If a source can no longer be opened, the saved passage stays so you can still see what was relied on.

ai.heading: What automated tools do and do not do
ai.body: Automated tools may search for sources and answer questions using only approved passages. They cannot verify a claim, decide who is at fault, change a status, or publish anything. Their answers are explanations, not sources, and always show the sources they used. If the sources do not answer a question, the answer says so.

scout.heading: Newly found sources
scout.body: Sources found by search are marked "discovered — not yet reviewed". They are not part of the record. A person decides whether one is added, and adding a source does not by itself make a statement true.

review.heading: Human review
review.body: A person reviews evidence before it changes a public record, and publishing is always a separate step from reviewing a report. Automated tools never publish.

reporting.heading: Reporting a concern
reporting.body: You can send a report without an account, email address, or phone number. Reports are private by default and are never published automatically. Only a reviewer can read them. Photos and files are cleaned of embedded details such as location before they are stored, and you may choose whether to leave contact details.
reporting.limit: This is a prototype. It is not an emergency service, it cannot promise a response or protection, and it should not be used to report danger. If someone is in danger, contact local emergency services first.

correct.heading: If something looks wrong
correct.body: If you think a record is incorrect, out of date, or missing a source, you can report it privately from that record. A reviewer decides what, if anything, changes. ShaidaGo cannot promise a particular outcome or timing.
